title: Opening principles
intro: The ideas behind every good opening: take the centre, develop your pieces, keep your king safe. Learn these before any particular opening.

lessons.title: Centre, development, castling
lessons.summary: Three rules that make every opening work.

steps.text: The four squares in the middle matter most. Pieces in the centre reach more squares, and pawns there take space from your opponent.
1.e4 takes a centre square and opens lines for the queen and the bishop on f1.
Develop: bring a knight or a bishop towards the centre.
steps.hint: Knights go to f3 or c3; the bishop can go to c4 or b5.
steps.ifWrong: Bring a knight or bishop off the back row, towards the centre.
steps.ifRight: Good development: a new piece joins the game.

feedback.g1h3: A knight on the edge reaches fewer squares. Head for the centre instead.
feedback.b1a3: A knight on the edge reaches fewer squares. Head for the centre instead.
feedback.d1h5: Bringing the queen out early lets Black chase her while developing. Develop a knight or bishop first.
feedback.d1f3: Bringing the queen out early lets Black chase her while developing. Develop a knight or bishop first.

steps.text: Here both sides have followed the rules: centre pawns, knights out, bishops out. The last job is to castle, so the king is safe and a rook comes towards the middle.
Finish your development: get your king to safety.
steps.hint: The squares between your king and the h1 rook are empty.
steps.ifWrong: That is not castling. Move the king two squares towards the h1 rook.
steps.ifRight: Castled. Centre, development, king safety: done.

lessons.title: Punish early mistakes
lessons.summary: An early queen and a weak f7 square.

steps.text: Black brings the queen out early. She takes a pawn, but now she stands in the middle where your pieces can attack her.
After 2...Qxd5 the queen is exposed. Every move that attacks her gains time.
Develop a piece and attack the queen at the same time.
steps.ifWrong: Find a developing move that attacks the queen.
steps.ifRight: The queen must move again, and you are a move ahead in development.

steps.text: Early on, f7 is protected only by Black's king. Here White's queen and bishop both aim at it, and Black has just attacked the queen with ...Nf6, forgetting about f7.
Punish the mistake: checkmate in one.
steps.hint: Capture on f7. The bishop protects your queen there.
steps.ifWrong: Look at f7: the queen can land there, protected by the bishop.
